rows: CCFL backlight lamp in the display
Toxic vapour; a few milligrams per lamp
Remove the CCFL lamp whole without breaking it, seal it in a glass jar, and hand it to an authorised e-waste recycler. If broken, ventilate, scoop debris, never vacuum.
Solder on circuit boards; units built before 1 July 2006 may contain leaded solder
Damages the nervous system; pollutes soil and water
Never desolder, burn or acid-wash the circuit boards. Send them whole to an authorised e-waste recycler, who safely recovers the lead along with gold, silver and copper.
6-cell or 9-cell main battery, plus CR-2032 coin cell

Never put it in the dustbin. Tape the terminals, bag each battery separately, and give it to a battery recycler. Swollen batteries must not be charged, pressed or punctured.
Plastic casing, circuit boards, cable insulation
Never burn the plastic casing or cables to recover copper, as this releases toxic fumes. Hand all plastics and cables to an authorised e-waste recycler for controlled processing.

ಸರ್ಕ್ಯೂಟ್ ಬೋರ್ಡ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಎಂದಿಗೂ ಡಿಸೋಲ್ಡರ್ ಮಾಡಬೇಡಿ, ಸುಡಬೇಡಿ ಅಥವಾ ಆಮ್ಲದಿಂದ ತೊಳೆಯಬೇಡಿ. ಅವುಗಳನ್ನು ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣವಾಗಿ ಅಧಿಕೃತ ಇ-ತ್ಯಾಜ್ಯ ಮರುಚಕ್ರೀಕರಣಕಾರರಿಗೆ ಕಳುಹಿಸಿ; ಅವರು ಚಿನ್ನ, ಬೆಳ್ಳಿ ಮತ್ತು ತಾಮ್ರದ ಜೊತೆಗೆ ಸೀಸವನ್ನೂ ಸುರಕ್ಷಿತವಾಗಿ ಮರುಪಡೆಯುತ್ತಾರೆ.

ತೂತಾದರೆ ಅಥವಾ ಶಾರ್ಟ್-ಸರ್ಕ್ಯೂಟ್ ಆದರೆ ಬೆಂಕಿಯ ಅಪಾಯ; ಕೋಬಾಲ್ಟ್ ವಿಷಕಾರಿ

ಇದನ್ನು ಎಂದಿಗೂ ಕಸದ ಬುಟ್ಟಿಗೆ ಹಾಕಬೇಡಿ. ಟರ್ಮಿನಲ್‌ಗಳಿಗೆ ಟೇಪ್ ಹಾಕಿ, ಪ್ರತಿ ಬ್ಯಾಟರಿಯನ್ನು ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕ ಚೀಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಇಡಿ, ಬ್ಯಾಟರಿ ಮರುಚಕ್ರೀಕರಣಕಾರರಿಗೆ ನೀಡಿ. ಉಬ್ಬಿದ ಬ್ಯಾಟರಿಗಳನ್ನು ಚಾರ್ಜ್ ಮಾಡಬಾರದು, ಒತ್ತಬಾರದು ಅಥವಾ ತೂತು ಮಾಡಬಾರದು.
ಪ್ಲಾಸ್ಟಿಕ್ ಕವಚ, ಸರ್ಕ್ಯೂಟ್ ಬೋರ್ಡ್‌ಗಳು, ಕೇಬಲ್ ನಿರೋಧನ

ತಾಮ್ರವನ್ನು ಪಡೆಯಲು ಪ್ಲಾಸ್ಟಿಕ್ ಕವಚ ಅಥವಾ ಕೇಬಲ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಎಂದಿಗೂ ಸುಡಬೇಡಿ, ಇದರಿಂದ ವಿಷಕಾರಿ ಹೊಗೆ ಹೊರಬರುತ್ತದೆ. ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಪ್ಲಾಸ್ಟಿಕ್ ಮತ್ತು ಕೇಬಲ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ನಿಯಂತ್ರಿತ ಸಂಸ್ಕರಣೆಗಾಗಿ ಅಧಿಕೃತ ಇ-ತ್ಯಾಜ್ಯ ಮರುಚಕ್ರೀಕರಣಕಾರರಿಗೆ ನೀಡಿ.

sections.title: 3. Carbon Footprint
sections.intro: A **carbon footprint** is the total amount of greenhouse gases (primarily carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide) generated directly and indirectly by an individual, organization, event, or product.

sections.title: Important scope and evidence note
sections.intro:
This passport uses the USHA instruction manual and the manufacturer's HC 812 T product page as the primary sources. Retail listings are used only where the manufacturer does not publish a value. Exact bill of materials, component weights and a model-specific life-cycle assessment were not found; therefore material descriptions and manufacturing-footprint discussion are identified as typical or indicative, not as verified measurements of this exact heater.

Model naming: USHA's manual calls the product FH 812T, while the manufacturer's current product page lists HC 812 T. This passport treats FH812T / HC 812T as the same 812T heat-convector family, but the model label on the physical unit should be checked.

sections.title: 3. Carbon Footprint and Energy Use
sections.intro:
A product carbon footprint includes raw-material extraction, component manufacture, assembly, transport, electricity consumed during use and end-of-life treatment. No verified FH812T-specific life-cycle assessment or manufacturer-declared carbon footprint was located. It would therefore be misleading to assign an exact total manufacturing or lifetime footprint to this model.

The use-phase electricity can be estimated from the rated power. For illustration, this calculation uses 0.716 kg CO₂/kWh, the Indian grid weighted-average factor stated in the CEA CO₂ Baseline Database User Guide for FY 2022–23. The factor changes over time and the actual result depends on the electricity mix and thermostat cycling.
sections.note: *Illustrative upper-bound-style calculation assumes the heater draws its full rated heating power for the entire period. The thermostat may switch the heating element off and reduce actual consumption; fan electricity is additional but comparatively small and is not separately included because the FH812T manual gives no fan wattage. The 2000 W rating is power, not energy consumed regardless of time.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.intro:
The USHA FH812T is a portable 1000 W / 2000 W heat convector with a built-in fan, adjustable thermostat, thermal cut-out, twin-turbo airflow design and adjustable stand. The manufacturer's manual is the strongest source for its electrical ratings and safety functions. Public product information does not establish an exact bill of materials, manufacturing carbon footprint or component-level material quantities, so these have been treated as unknown or typical rather than stated as measured facts.

Its largest controllable environmental impact during ownership is likely to be electricity use. At the 2000 W setting, one hour of full-power operation uses about 2 kWh; using the CEA FY 2022–23 grid factor gives an illustrative 1.432 kg CO₂ per hour. Actual emissions depend on operating time, thermostat cycling and the grid factor for the year of use. The most practical circular-economy actions are to use the thermostat sensibly, maintain the appliance, repair it through authorised service where viable, and route an unusable heater through formal e-waste collection.
